_comment: Live Lab (systems/lab.gd, .scratch/lab-port/spec.md) -- provisional numbers, tagged for balance. procedures.<recipeKey> (calc spent per item = the recipe's data/recipes.json ingredients, the single source): baseTolerance = band half-width before widening; ideal = the authored perfect procedure (apparatus = data/approaches.json id, ore = an ingredient ore that must be in the mixture for the step to match, absent for a step that works the existing mixture, target on a 0-100 gauge, weight; weights sum to 100); base = the procedure a newly granted recipe knows, its steps' calc summing to the recipe's ingredients, every ingredient ore in some step; hints = the hidden steps, each naming the ideal step index it reveals (a base step matching that ideal step gets its target corrected, otherwise the ideal step is inserted, no calc) and one rung (hint1, hint2, master). A vague hint shows a region of the band widened by vagueSpread each side and shifted by its offset (|offset| <= vagueSpread, so the band always sits inside); an exact hint shows the true band. rankThresholds[i] is the minimum score for rank i+1. skillFactor, benchBonusFactors: band_half_width = baseTolerance x (1 + skillFactor x craftingSkill) x (1 + benchBonus), benchBonus = home x Home workshop bonus + perk x Guild craft-chance perk + attunement x seated Movement attunement (when its ore is an ingredient). A finished run scores sum(weight x accuracy) - extraStepPenalty per extra step + ladyScorePerLevel x Be A Lady level, clamped 0-100; a cracked or abandoned run gives xpReward / failedRunXpDivisor XP. staffTierCap = the highest tier a Lab staffer's items come out at (tier = their crafting level, capped here). gauges: per-apparatus gauge settings (a compress released at or past crackAt cracks the vessel; grinding strokes; distilling drips fall over fallMsec, one every beatMsec). gauges.*.directionWords = the clue's ~ direction for a reading below (higher) or above (lower) the ideal target. vagueToExactHits = in-band runs on a vague step that make it exact; clueText = per-step clue marks (hit/near/none/changed) and learn suffixes (towardExact takes hits so far and vagueToExactHits). bonus: a finished run at rank >= best rank rolls chance, then picks one of types at random (extraItems added, refundFraction of the run's calc back, xpMultiplier on the run's XP). badRun: a finished run scoring below scoreBelow returns one of lines, one time in oneIn. PROSE-REVIEW: every hints label/note, directionWords, clueText and badRun.lines entry is new copy.

vague.note: Compress it a bit longer.

exact.note: Compress to 82. Stop well short of the red line.

vague.note: Grind it once between the press and the heat.

exact.note: Grind between the press and the heat, mid-swing.

vague.note: Give it one more press once it's off the heat. Not a hard one.

exact.note: Off the heat, press to 30 and let go.

vague.note: Heat it a bit hotter.

exact.note: Heat to 62, not 40.

vague.note: Finish with a distil. Catch the drips somewhere in the middle.

exact.note: Finish with a distil: four drips, each caught halfway.

vague.note: Grind it again once it's warm. Late, not early.

exact.note: Off the heat, grind again, late in the swing.

vague.note: Distil it between the press and the heat.

exact.note: Distil between the press and the heat, drips caught halfway.

vague.note: Heat it lower than you'd think.

exact.note: Heat to 35. Lower than you'd think.

vague.note: One last grind after the heat. Don't wait for the swing.

exact.note: Off the heat, grind early in the swing.

vague.note: The second press wants less than you're giving it.

exact.note: Second press to 20. Barely a squeeze.

vague.note: Distil it before it sees any heat. Catch the drips early.

exact.note: Distil between the first press and the heat, drips caught a little early.

vague.note: It isn't finished after the last press. Grind it, late-ish.

exact.note: After the last press, grind past the middle of the swing.

vague.note: It wants more heat than that.

exact.note: Heat to 70.

vague.note: Distil it a second time, off the heat. Catch these later.

exact.note: Distil again after the heat, drips caught past halfway.

vague.note: Give it a press before the second distil. Not much of one.

exact.note: Between the heat and the second distil, press to 45.

vague.note: The second grind comes too early in the swing.

exact.note: Second grind, late in the swing. Near the end.

vague.note: Finish with a press. Firm, not hard.

exact.note: After the second grind, press to 55.

vague.note: Warm it between the grinds. Barely warm.

exact.note: Between the grinds, heat to 30 and no further.

vague.note: It wants a lot more heat than that.

exact.note: Heat to 80. Hot as you dare.

vague.note: Press it again once it's hot. Harder than the first time.

exact.note: After the heat, press to 80.

vague.note: Break it up before it sees the heat. Early in the swing.

exact.note: Between the first press and the heat, grind early in the swing.

vague.note: The grind's coming too early in the swing.

exact.note: Grind late in the swing. Past the middle.

vague.note: Press it after the grind. Middling pressure.

exact.note: After the grind, press to 45.

vague.note: One more go on the heat at the end. Gently.

exact.note: After the last press, heat to 25 and take it off.

vague.note: The second press wants more. Nearly all of it.

exact.note: Second press to 88. Stop before it cracks.

vague.note: Grind it once it's pressed. Mid-swing, roughly.

exact.note: After the second press, grind right in the middle of the swing.

vague.note: Finish on the heat, but only just.

exact.note: Last of all, heat to 15. Hardly a flicker.

clueText.changed: That step made a difference. Another go and maybe you can improve it.

lines: The mixture sets into something the colour of a bruise. You bin it, and the spoon.
The flask makes a small, polite noise and then a less polite one. The bench will need a new mat.
Whatever this was going to be, it has decided against it.
It smells of burnt hair and Tuesday. You open a window and write nothing down.
The calc goes grey and stays grey. Somewhere, a ledger notes the loss.
